question.text: During periods of no market dislocation, the Corporate Debt Market Development Fund invests in:

explanation.text: The Logic: When there is no market dislocation, CDMDF invests in liquid and low-risk debt instruments in a manner specified by SEBI. Its primary purpose — purchasing corporate debt securities from debt-oriented mutual fund schemes — is activated only during periods of market dislocation. The Trap: The fund doesn't sit idle during normal market conditions. It maintains a liquid, low-risk portfolio that can be quickly deployed when market stress occurs. Note: The dual mode — passive low-risk holdings in normal markets and active dislocation-period purchases — is what makes CDMDF an effective backstop mechanism.
